prompts.rubber_cracks_v2:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: one production PBR scalar mask texture for aged cracked industrial rubber. This is raw numerical material data, not a lit photograph, object, or render. Generate a very detailed 2048 by 2048 square opaque grayscale bitmap.
Subject: authentic, clearly readable stress fissures in old black rubber. Pure black represents the intact level rubber. White represents the deepest open center of a fissure, medium gray shallower fissure margins and thin secondary branches. Make several irregular localized families of branching cracks with distinct long stress fractures, medium crooked splits and thinner fading branch tips. Nonuniform natural widths, about 3–12 pixels for most substantial cracks and 1–3 pixels for secondary tips at 2048 resolution, with just a few wider open splits. Longer major cracks run about 15–35 percent of the image width before branching or fading. Edges are torn and slightly jagged with fine imperfections, never perfectly straight. Crack families have different directions and varied local densities. Between them leave significant irregular areas of completely intact black rubber. About 8–15 percent visibly cracked coverage, with long open fissures readable even at reduced size. A small amount of local parallel stress cracking is plausible, but avoid repeating parallel grooves. Rough depth transitions across fissures should be narrow and detailed, so a height channel can form recessed torn edges. The result should resemble actual aged tire sidewall or elastomer deterioration, with fewer decisive cracks and some broad unbroken areas.
Composition: square edge-to-edge orthographic flat texture map of an infinite continuous surface, seamless repeating across all four borders. Values are scalar coverage/depth only. Grayscale only, black background and gray-to-white fissure paths.
Avoid: uniform polygon cells, Voronoi crack web, all-over crocodile skin plates, dried mud or ceramic crazing, regular tile shapes, decorative lightning bolts, veins on a leaf, broad gray clouds, lighting, shadows, bevel shading, reflections, material colors, metallic sparkle, borders, margins, text, labels, collages, rendered spheres. No tiny indiscernible noise masquerading as the main cracks.
prompts.grease_deposits_v2:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: a production PBR grayscale coverage mask for accumulated grease, oily handling grime and wiped deposits on industrial machinery. Generate one sharply detailed 2048 by 2048 square opaque grayscale texture. This is raw scalar numerical data, NOT a photograph of shiny metal, and has absolutely no lighting or reflections.
Pixel semantics: pure black means clean surface. Gray means thin or partly wiped grease film. White means thickest greasy deposit. White and gray values describe actual deposited matter, not specular shine. Create a mostly black map with a few substantial irregular deposits, smaller localized rubbed smears and quiet clean regions, about 20–35 percent visible overall coverage. Distinct, readable shapes, with very fine material detail inside them.
Pattern: believable patches of mechanical grease displaced by repeated handling and cloth wiping. Uneven elongated smudges and irregular pressed patches with dark wiped-through gaps, streaky softened boundaries, and localized thick gathered residue at the ends of dragging motion. A few broad organic wipe arcs with multiple finer slightly broken striations inside them; other deposits dragged diagonally and vertically. A couple of subtle partial handling impressions can have delicate parallel friction ridges, but no complete regular oval or circular fingerprint stamps. Mix a few large irregular 15–30 percent-image-width wiped patches with medium smears and sparse tiny residue flecks. The patches must vary drastically in size, density, direction and shape. Some interrupted thin trails connect neighboring residue patches; several areas stay completely black. Fine clotted/granular deposit texture in the thicker patches, not generic grain everywhere.
Composition: flat orthographic edge-to-edge map of an infinite surface. Seamless repeating at all four borders, square full canvas. Only grayscale; uniform clean background black.
Avoid: smoky cloud fields, fog, uniform gray backdrop, polished chrome highlights, directional light, shadows, metallic reflections, vignettes, dirt-colored photographs, repeating circular stamps or repeated fingerprints, evenly spaced dots, symmetrical patterns, tire tracks, painted brush icons, thick regular stripes, perspective, object silhouettes, labels, text, borders, renders of spheres, multi-panel grids. Grease deposit boundaries should look rubbed and smeared by real contact, not spraypaint or crumpled paper.

refinements.rubber_cracks_v2:
Edit target: the supplied grayscale rubber-crack image. Preserve the exact crack network, individual large and small crack trajectories, locations, widths and branching topology. Change only the scalar value interpretation so this is a TRUE UNLIT GRAYSCALE MASK instead of the shaded crack photograph it currently resembles.
The entire interior of every open fissure must be bright: fill the dark centers enclosed by the existing bright crack edges to gray-white. The deepest centers must be WHITE and the narrow margins taper through GRAY toward the PURE BLACK intact surface. Brightest values must lie down the middle of each crack, never only along a raised rim. No black slit inside a white crack. No highlights, bevel shading or dark centers. Larger cracks should have a continuous white interior with subtly varied grayscale depth, smaller branches lower intensity, branching tips fade to black. Keep sharp ragged path boundaries and varying widths. Preserve large clean black areas between crack families; remove background grain so intact rubber is truly black. Do not thicken the paths or add branches. Seamless tile requested, square bitmap, preserve full-canvas topology, no labels or borders. This will be applied as negative height to carve genuine dark recesses into black rubber, so white means CUT DEPTH and must include the center of the crack.
